headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading workflow errors when ctx observes and n8n executes shared filesystem/API-driven outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code PostToolUse and Stop events and touches filesystem/MCP-related context, while n8n can read/write server filesystem and drive workflows via integrations. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if ctx output is later ingested by n8n or copied into a workflow. The exact bridge is not fully documented, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF ctx output is ingested into an n8n workflow node as text or JSON
IF n8n workflows parse ctx-generated files or logs as instructions
mitigations: Add a strict schema validator before any n8n node consumes ctx output
Separate ctx and n8n workspaces at the filesystem level
Disable any workflow step that treats free-form text as commands
Log and review all ctx-to-n8n handoffs for prompt-like content
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to ctx outputs and enforce them in n8n

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, graph data, and MCP servers; n8n processes whatever the workflow handles and has broad network egress plus server filesystem access. If the same workspace or credentials are shared, sensitive context can flow from ctx into n8n and then out through integrations. The profiles do not prove a default shared workspace, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF ctx writes logs or graph data into a directory that n8n reads
IF an n8n workflow sends ctx-derived files or records to an external integration
mitigations: Restrict n8n credentials to least privilege
Move ctx logs and graph data to a separate directory
Mask secrets before n8n ingests any ctx artifact
Review outbound n8n nodes for sensitive destinations
requires-engineering: enforce per-data-class egress policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can use filesystem and MCP surfaces, while n8n can execute shell commands, write the server filesystem, and spawn subprocesses. Both also support multiple instances, and n8n explicitly shares state via datastore/connected systems. If they target the same mutable paths or workflow state, concurrent writes and race conditions can corrupt artifacts or overwrite each other; the profiles do not show locking.
conditions: IF ctx and n8n write to the same directory or datastore
IF n8n Execute Command nodes mutate files that ctx also updates
mitigations: Assign disjoint filesystem roots to ctx and n8n
Disable n8n Execute Command for shared paths
Serialize writes with an external lock file
Run a quick audit for overlapping writable directories
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx is a context-management agent that observes tool events, and n8n is a workflow orchestrator whose AI Agent node can call tools. If n8n consumes ctx-produced summaries or recommendations without verification, errors can cascade into automated actions across integrations. Because n8n has broad egress and action-taking authority, the blast radius can be irreversible.
conditions: IF n8n AI Agent nodes treat ctx output as authoritative
IF ctx summaries are forwarded into n8n actions without a human verification step
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before any n8n action
Require n8n to verify ctx claims against source data
Limit n8n workflows to read-only actions until reviewed
Add explicit confidence fields to ctx outputs
requires-engineering: implement policy gates before tool execution

E_compliance.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs and graph data, while n8n processes arbitrary workflow data and stores secrets per-credential on its server. That combination can create retention and residency mismatches if regulated data enters n8n workflows. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR/FedRAMP status, so I cite the documented data-handling surfaces rather than inventing a specific regime.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into ctx logs or graph data
IF n8n workflows retain or export that data beyond the source system's policy
mitigations: Classify data before it enters either system
Shorten n8n retention for workflow executions
Avoid storing regulated data in ctx logs
Review credential and secret storage settings
requires-engineering: map residency and retention controls end to end
